# derived from monero v0.18.5.1 source, not captured from a run
# ONE OBJECT PER ROW OF address::PREFIXES (DESIGN.md §5b), and a unit test asserts the two have the
# SAME ROW COUNT, so adding a form to one without the other fails the build (§1b.1). THE NINE FORMS.
# THIS IS THE FILE THAT MAKES THE FCMP++ / CARROT FORK A ONE-LINE CHANGE: when a v17 fork ships new
# address forms, adding each one is ONE row in PREFIXES plus ONE object here -- no `if`, no new
# function, no change to any caller (§1b.1, §5b).
#
# KEYS: { net, kind, prefix, leading, len, example } -- exactly the six DESIGN.md §8 Phase 0 names.
#
# `prefix` -- the base58 prefix VARINT, src/cryptonote_config.h:227-229 (mainnet), :270-272 (testnet),
#   :285-287 (stagenet). All nine are below 128, so each is a single varint byte.
#     CRYPTONOTE_PUBLIC_ADDRESS_BASE58_PREFIX             18 / 53 / 24
#     CRYPTONOTE_PUBLIC_INTEGRATED_ADDRESS_BASE58_PREFIX  19 / 54 / 25
#     CRYPTONOTE_PUBLIC_SUBADDRESS_BASE58_PREFIX          42 / 63 / 36
#
# `len` -- follows from Monero's base58, which encodes in BLOCKS: encoded_block_sizes[] =
#   {0,2,3,5,6,7,9,10,11} (src/common/base58.cpp:48), i.e. 8 bytes -> 11 characters and a trailing
#   partial block of 5 bytes -> 7. So:
#     standard / subaddress: 1 prefix + 32 public spend + 32 public view + 4 checksum = 69 bytes
#                            = 8 full blocks + 5 -> 8*11 + 7 =  95 characters
#     integrated:            the same plus an 8-byte payment id                       = 77 bytes
#                            = 9 full blocks + 5 -> 9*11 + 7 = 106 characters
#   The 4-byte checksum is the first 4 bytes of Keccak-256 over the preceding bytes. address::parse
#   does NOT verify it -- DESIGN.md §3.1 takes no Keccak dependency, because §2a.6 gets a stronger
#   guarantee from validate_address for free -- so a string can pass address::parse and still be a
#   bad address. validate_address-invalid.json is exactly that string.
#
# `leading` IS AN ARRAY BECAUSE THE LEADING CHARACTER IS A SET, NOT A CHARACTER (§1b.8). It is the
#   base58 digit of the WHOLE FIRST 8-BYTE BLOCK -- the prefix varint plus the first SEVEN bytes of
#   the public spend key -- so for some prefixes the block value straddles a digit boundary. Dividing
#   each prefix's block range [p<<56, (p<<56)|0x00FF_FFFF_FFFF_FFFF] by 58^10 over Monero's alphabet
#   (123456789ABCDEFGHJKLMNPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijkmnopqrstuvwxyz, base58.cpp:46) gives the sets below.
#   RECOMPUTED FOR THIS FILE, not copied: eight prefixes yield one digit and TESTNET STANDARD (53)
#   yields TWO, '9' and 'A'. The switch happens when the first seven key bytes reach
#   0xceb74b07d8c400, i.e. for roughly one testnet standard address in five -- so a hard
#   leading-character check would reject about 20% of them. address::parse therefore uses `leading`
#   only as a display hint and as a fast reject WHEN THE SET HAS ONE MEMBER; length and base58
#   decodability decide, and the decoded prefix varint names the form.
#   NOTE mainnet standard and mainnet integrated share '4', and stagenet standard and stagenet
#   integrated share '5': within a network the leading character does NOT distinguish standard from
#   integrated at all -- only `len` does.
#
# `example` -- EVERY ONE IS A REAL, CHECKSUM-VALID ADDRESS TAKEN FROM MONERO'S OWN TEST SUITE, not
#   synthesised, so each is a valid input to a real monero-wallet-rpc `validate_address` as well as to
#   address::parse. Eight come from one upstream table,
#   tests/functional_tests/validate_address.py:67-81, where upstream asserts for each the very
#   net/integrated/subaddress verdict recorded here (:85-90); the mainnet subaddress
#   (888tNkZrPN...) is src/simplewallet/simplewallet.h:56, upstream's donate@getmonero.org address,
#   which validate_address.py:97-107 asserts is mainnet and `subaddress`.
#     mainnet  standard   validate_address.py:68
#     mainnet  integrated validate_address.py:72
#     mainnet  subaddress simplewallet.h:56
#     testnet  standard   validate_address.py:70
#     testnet  integrated validate_address.py:75
#     testnet  subaddress validate_address.py:76
#     stagenet standard   validate_address.py:71
#     stagenet integrated validate_address.py:78
#     stagenet subaddress validate_address.py:79
#   Each example's first character was checked against its `leading` set and each decodes to `len`
#   characters and to `prefix` as its first varint byte. THE TESTNET STANDARD EXAMPLE BEGINS '9', the
#   first member of its two-element set; no upstream vector begins 'A' for that form, so the 'A' half
#   of the set is proved by the arithmetic above and not by an example. A test that asserts
#   `example[0] == leading[0]` would pass today and is the wrong assertion; the right one is
#   `leading.contains(example[0])`.
